route: IMPORT_CAD <density> TRUE 80 <iges>; CONVERT_CAD_TO_MESH -1; SAVEAS; EXPORT_SURFACE_MESH OBJ -1; the IGES imported directly, as the geometry build runs it
geometry: synthetic, generated by the library (no research or employer mesh)
launch: hidden, one process at a time of this lane, free RAM 1.6 to 4.0 GB before each run, peak FlightStream working set about 0.9 GB (sampled 837 MB, 1681 MB for the two builds sampled; other sessions share the machine)

runs.geometry: one lifting surface, NACA 0012, sref 0.24 m2, AR 6, taper 0.5, sweep 15 deg (4 IGES faces)
two lifting surfaces named WING and TAIL in one IGES
one body of revolution, length 2.0 m
the wing, with the instruction renaming Model 0 to demo (SURFACE_RENAME 1 demo before the save)
runs.read_back: passed: the saved boundaries equal the instruction's

findings: The importer names the one body it converts 'Model 0' whatever the members of the IGES are: a one member and a two member file both save one boundary and one OBJ object named 'Model 0'. The names of the IGES components (406 NAME levels) are not boundaries of the saved model.
A boundary name cannot carry a space (the instruction model refuses it), so the native instruction renames 'Model 0' to one word.

The audit G1 of the geometry build fails on the importer's own tessellation of the generated wing (triangles of zero area on the blunt trailing edge strip, x near the trailing edge, z near 0) at LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH density, and on the body (edges of more than two faces, zero-area faces); a failed audit promotes nothing, so no .fsm reaches the row.
